Research Verdict

Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) reliably achieves a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 1
000–1300 W/mK in standard high-purity single crystals [1][2][
10], while recent isotopic enrichment and arsenic purification push measured values to ~1500 W/mK [3] and potentially
above 2100 W/mK [4]. On the weight of the above, ~130
0 W/mK is a well-replicated benchmark for natural-abundance chemical-vapor-transport crystals rather than an intrinsic material

ceiling.

## Theory predictions
c1 excluded — agent timeout, no finding. Including four-phonon scattering reduces ab initio predictions from ~220
0 to 1400 W/mK [5], though 2025 calculations incorporating temperature-dependent force constants revise natural

c-BAs predictions down to ~1061 W/mK [6].

## Measurement history
In July 20
18, three independent groups published back-to-back *Science* papers establishing 300 K thermal conductivity between ~100
0 and 1300 W/mK via TDTR [1][2][3]. Subsequent optical transient
grating and improved growth studies confirmed 1200–1300 W/mK in low-defect
regions [10][11], while isotopically enriched crystals reached ~1500 W/mK [

3].

## Sample and methods
Although point defects and impurities scatter phonons [7], higher-purity synthesis refutes a hard
1300 W/mK ceiling [3][4]. Meanwhile, TDTR studies remain divided over whether quasi-ballistic phonon
transport suppresses apparent conductivity at small laser spot sizes [8] or yields bulk diffusive values without spot-size dependence [9
/mK thermal conductivity and 1600 cm²/Vs ambipolar carrier mobility at the same sample locations
[10]. While specialized growth has produced crystals larger than 4×2×1 mm [13], typical

bulk crystals remain limited to ~1 mm scales with non-uniform quality, preventing wafer-scale deployment [12].

## Contested & ruled
- **c2 (Theory):** Advocates showed four-phonon scattering lowers predictions to 1400 W/m
K [5], whereas Skeptics cited 2025 revisions down to 1060.5

1 W/mK [6].
- **c5 (Intrinsic ceiling & defects):** Advocates showed impurities quench conductivity below 1300 W
/mK [1][7], while Skeptics cited isotopically enriched (~1500 W/mK
) [3] and purified-arsenic (>2100 W/mK) crystals [4]. *Per human ruling: "b"

— "rule for the counter-evidence"*.
- **c6 (TDTR artifacts):** Advocates showed ballistic transport decreases TDTR readings
[8], while Skeptics cited 2018 tests showing no spot-size dependence from 5.

4 to 12.6 μm [9].
- **Tie-breaker (c7):** Additional investigation confirmed
multiple laboratories achieved >1300 W/mK and ~1500 W/mK in high

-purity crystals [3][11].

- c2 — CONTESTED (0.55)

88)

- c6 — CONTESTED (0.50)

- c7 — SUPPORTED (0.85)
- c8 — SUPPORTED (0.90)
- c9 — SUPPORT

ED (0.75)
